extracted.intended_audience: scholars and academics invited to peer review for the American Political Science Review (APSR)
extracted.subtask_short: APSR peer review for journal articles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academics performing peer review for submissions to the American Political Science Review, including procedural notes and pointers to resources on ethics and how to review. Aimed at helping reviewers produce constructive, rigorous, and transferable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous and ethical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the foundation of quality in research for both books and journals, ensuring that published research is rigorous and ethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate submissions for methodological rigor and adherence to ethical standards. The page points reviewers to the 'Ethics in peer review' resource for further guidance on ethical responsibilities during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide forward-looking advice
rubrics_metrics.description: We advise reviewers to provide forward-looking advice to the authors, even if they believe that the submitted manuscript belongs to another journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the APSR allows authors to transfer reviews to another journal (Review Transfer Policy), reviewers should offer constructive, actionable suggestions authors can use to improve the manuscript regardless of fit; avoid only recommending rejection without guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers can access a number of resources to assist them with their peer reviewing duties: 'How to peer review journal articles: a practical introduction to conducting peer reviews, especially for those who are new to the process'; 'Ethics in peer review'; 'Online peer review systems, and how to anonymously annotate manuscripts'; 'Peer review FAQs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or experienced reviewers should consult these linked resources for practical how-to advice, ethical rules, technical instructions for annotation, and frequently asked questions. The journal recommends these resources as aids in producing high-quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the journal's online submission/annotation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal partners with a secure submission system to handle manuscript submissions; reviewers will need an account for the submission system (separate from Cambridge Core) and can use online peer review systems to anonymously annotate manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must register for and use the partner submission system to access manuscripts and submit reviews; for login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages. Use the anonymous annotation tools where provided to protect confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the Editorial Office for support or questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal administrator is also happy to help with any queries regarding undertaking peer review assignments. Please contact the Editorial Office with any questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For procedural or policy questions, contact apsr@apsanet.org or the Editorial Office. The administrator can assist with assignment queries, system problems, or clarification of review expectations.
